title.narrative: Support Member States to address socioeconomic challenges of climate change

description.narrative: This activity is designed to address multidimensional challenges resulting from climate-induced events, and support Member States in Southern Africa in addressing them with appropriate policy responses, and other resilient measures. In line with the orientation and results framework of Output 2.2, the primary intervention will develop actions to investigate the nexus between climate change and its socioeconomic consequences on vulnerable populations and their communities. Specifically, it will support community-based research activities on the impact of climate change and environmental disasters on patterns of migration in Southern Africa, zeroing in on youth migration (with disaggregation of demographic data based on gender and other vulnerable groups such as persons with disabilities), in transboundary communities, bordering Zimbabwe and Mozambique, as one cluster, and Lesotho and South Africa, as the second cluster. Data collected and knowledge generated from the respective research activities will contribute to informing multistakeholder engagements and dialogues, bringing together communities and decisionmakers at both subnational and national levels, aimed at influencing the development and/or reform of social policies related to health, education and housing, etc., and strategies related to disaster risk reduction in affected countries. In addition to Output 2.2 as its main area of contribution, this activity will also, among others, contribute to Output 3.4 as a secondary result area, and leverage close working relationships with SC sector's work on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), and CI sector’s work on community radios. This intervention will result in the development of concrete knowledge products, including research reports, policy papers and briefs, interactive maps and so forth, thus providing foundational background documentation for convening multistakeholder policy dialogues and engagements alluded to earlier. The initiative will deploy the tools and frameworks being developed by MOST programme to support and improve public policies, especially in relation to climate and environment. Concretely, Climate Policy Toolkit based on the 2025 Report "Who Bears the Costs? Addressing Inequalities from Climate Change and Climate Action," and the Policy Framework and Toolkit for the use of humanities to improve environmental policies, being developed through the BRIDGES coalition.
